kicker: Local video dubbing, stage by stage

scenes.headline: How a video gets dubbed on your own machine
scenes.sub: One open-source studio, from separation to timing
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cadence! Let's follow one video through an open-source dubbing studio on your own machine.

scenes.text: Every stage can run on your own GPU, and a timing planner splits each overrun between faster audio and slower video.
scenes.say: The idea: every stage runs locally, and a planner shares each overrun between faster audio and slower video.

steps.say: First, a separation model pulls the voices away from the music.
Speech recognition writes down every word, its timing, and who spoke it.
For each speaker, it cuts five to fifteen seconds of clean speech to clone.
Each line is translated offline, with its time budget.
The voice model speaks every line in that speaker's voice.
Each line is fitted to its slot and laid over the original music.

scenes.title: How the voice model fills in speech

steps.label: all masked
steps.say: The voice model sees speech as a grid: eight token rows, one column per moment.

steps.label: surest first
steps.say: Each round, a transformer fills the blanks it is surest of.

steps.label: coarse rows first
steps.say: Coarse rows settle before fine ones.

steps.label: done
steps.note: the length was fixed before it started
steps.say: After sixteen rounds the grid is full. Its length was fixed up front, so a dub can ask for an exact duration.

scenes.title: Splitting an overrun
scenes.say: When a translation runs long, the planner splits the damage.

parts.note: spoken length divided by the slot
parts.say: Need is the line's length over its slot. Up to one point two, only the audio speeds up.
Past that, audio speeds up by the square root, at most one and a half.
Video slows by the rest, at most twice. Anything left stops the render.

steps.say: This picker decides whether your script leaves the machine.

scenes.label: licence records in the project's own inventory
scenes.say: The catch: the default voice weights are non-commercial, and the project clears nothing for commercial use.

scenes.text: The dubbing really runs locally and fits timing with care, but the default voice is licensed for non-commercial use only.
scenes.say: So the dubbing runs locally and fits timing with care. But the default voice is non-commercial.

recap: Overruns split between audio and video
scenes.say: Separate, transcribe, translate, speak, fit. Then check the licence.
